subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A pupil who can read and understand content well but produces illegible handwriting, struggles with spelling and letter-spacing, and finds the physical act of writing exhausting and slow, most likely has:
explanation: Dysgraphia specifically impairs written expression (handwriting, spelling, organising thoughts on paper) despite normal reading comprehension — distinct from dyslexia (reading), dyscalculia (mathematics), or dyspraxia (motor coordination more broadly).
